text: This is the single most important model in the whole project. int_active_members answers, once, the exact question Finance, Marketing, and Product have each been answering differently for years: was this person an active member today?

Two real edge cases caused the original disagreement: a membership paused in the middle of a month, and a member holding overlapping memberships at two different studio locations. Both get handled here, explicitly, in code.
A date-spine join expands every membership status period into one row per member per day, so a pause on the fourteenth shows up starting on the fourteenth -- not smeared across the whole month.

A window function then collapses any day where a member has more than one overlapping membership down to exactly one row, preferring an active status on a tie -- a written business rule, not a silent default.
One governed definition now exists. Next: the tests that make sure it stays correct every single night, not just today.
